children: At least two people died in the Grand Canyon and one person remained missing on Tuesday after a weekend of punishing rain flooded portions of the Arizona park.

Sections of Grand Canyon National Park were closed this week as teams searched for the missing person and meteorologists said thunderstorms were possible, along with the chance of more rain throughout the week.
Dozens of people were evacuated and two bodies were found after heavy rains hit the canyon over the weekend, the National Park Service said.

Authorities asked the public to help identify hikers and backpackers who were in the Bright Angel Canyon and Phantom Ranch areas of the park when the flooding occurred. The floods also damaged a mileslong pipeline that supplies water to the park.

August is the height of monsoon season in northern Arizona, where the Grand Canyon is located. Forecasters last weekend had issued flash-flood warnings for the area and said certain spots "can become raging killer currents in a matter of minutes."
